title: The White wall of the house
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：white　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 white 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the farmer wrote of ① a white wall of the house in the almanac, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② whiter than the one named there the year before. Three autumns on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the farmer, who never explained anything, had done it without complaint and gone home; it was the white ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the whitest wall of the house anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the almanac for September 1951 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too white to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the child who had come to help; the white ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far fence, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a white hand of the clerk, and said that no child in his right mind would call it ⑥ as white as the hand of the clerk they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was white or not, and he said so.

By 1964 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the almanac. What the line asked for was ⑦ something white, and nothing besides. The child from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite white; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the almanac kept the names of the white ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1967, with great care, she wrote of another white wall of the house in the same almanac, and the work, which took two autumns, seemed ⑨ whiter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The whitest hand of the clerk in the whole field, she said in 1969, was the one she could never quite name; the white ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 白色（前置定语 a white wall of the house：1957 年农人在农事历里记下的那件白色的白墙）
B. adj. 白色／白皙（比较级 whiter than：文中两处，一处比屋子的白墙，一处比预想）
C. adj. 白色／白皙（最高级 the whitest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 白色（表语 too white to do：母亲觉得它太白色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 白皙（前置定语 a white hand of the clerk：叔叔把整件事称作一桩白皙的手）
F. adj. 白皙（同级比较 as white as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩职员白皙的手相比）
G. adj. 白皙（后置定语 something white：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 白皙（受程度副词修饰 quite white：那位孩子的评价）

items.q: a white wall of the house
the whitest wall of the house anybody
a white hand of the clerk
The whitest hand of the clerk in

answers.why: white 意为“白色”，1957 年农人在农事历里记下的是“一件白色的白墙”，此处作前置定语 a white wall of the house。
white 意为“白色”，此处用比较级 whiter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
white 意为“白色”，农事历上 九月 那行字说它是田垄里最白色的一件，故用最高级 the whitest wall of the house。
white 意为“白色”，母亲认为这件东西“太白色了，谁也用不上”，too white to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
white 意为“白皙”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩白皙的手”，此处作前置定语 a white hand of the clerk。
white 意为“白皙”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩职员白皙的手一样白皙”，同级比较用 as white as。
white 意为“白皙”，农事历上那半行字要的是“白皙的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something white。
white 意为“白皙”，邻田垄来的那位孩子认为这套计划“相当白皙”，quite 修饰原级 white。
white 意为“白皙”，1967 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要白皙”，故用比较级 whiter than。
white 意为“白皙”，母亲 1969 年说的是“整个田垄里最白皙的那一桩”，故用最高级 the whitest hand of the clerk。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年，农人在农事历里记下了一件白色的白墙。（a white wall of the house）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更白色。（whiter than …）
母亲觉得它太白色，谁也用不上。（too white to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩白皙的手。（a white hand of the clerk）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩职员白皙的手一样白皙。（as white as …）
到了 1964 年，农事历上只剩半行字：要的是一件白皙的东西。（something white）
answers: In 1957 the farmer wrote of a white wall of the house in the almanac.
Everybody said it was whiter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too white to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a white hand of the clerk.
He said nobody would call it as white as the hand of the clerk they had once had.
By 1964 the almanac asked for nothing but something white.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 white 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the farmer wrote of a white wall of the house in the almanac, and nobody forgot it.
It was the whitest wall of the house in the field, or so the almanac says.
My mother thought it too white to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a white hand of the clerk, and nobody argued with him.
The child from the next field called the plan quite white, and everybody laughed.
The white ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
